sections.title: What the participle does
sections.content: You know the *-va/-ve* participle from B1 Unit 29 and from C1 Unit 16. This lesson uses it to describe layout: the participle says how a street or building lies or runs, and the main clause says what it does: *hossztengelyében elnyúlva* (stretching along its long axis), *sugarasan szétágazva* (branching out like rays), *szintkülönbséget áthidalva* (bridging a difference in height), *merőlegesen metszve* (cutting at right angles).

sections.title: Subject and comma
sections.content: Example: *Az Andrássy út hossztengelyében elnyúlva köti össze a belvárost a Városligettel.* The participle has the same subject as the main clause and is set off by a comma. *Merőlegesen* and *sugarasan* are adverbs of manner in *-an/-en*.

sections.title: Patterns in Context
rows: A sugárutak a belvárosból kiindulva sugarasan ágaznak szét a peremkerületek felé.
Starting from the city centre, the avenues branch out like rays towards the outer districts.
A sikló a meredek lejtőt áthidalva viszi fel az utasokat a Várhoz.
The funicular carries passengers up to the Castle, bridging the steep slope.
Az utcák a főutat merőlegesen metszve nyílnak a térre.
The streets open onto the square, cutting the main road at right angles.
